headline: A VMware vCenter zero-day used in espionage and four newly exploited flaws need patching now
plain_summary: Google says a suspected China-linked group used a previously unknown flaw in VMware vCenter, and a patch is available. CISA added four flaws to its list of exploited bugs; three have a federal deadline of 21 November. Cisco Expressway and Apache Roller flaws are also reported as exploited. Organisations running these products should patch; others need no action.

items.title: Google: vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 used in espionage campaign
items.why: Google Threat Intelligence Group attributes exploitation of an unauthenticated authentication bypass to a suspected PRC-nexus actor.
items.action: Apply the Broadcom patch for CVE-2026-123890 to vCenter Server now, restrict inbound access and egress from vCenter, and hunt with the GTIG indicators and the Mandiant VCSA hardening tool.

items.title: CISA adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap to exploited list
items.why: CISA cites evidence of active exploitation for all four flaws.
items.action: Find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. Axis 1.x is end of life with no fix (migrate or apply the July 12, 2026 commit); keep Axis, LiteLLM and REDCap off the open internet until addressed.

items.title: Cisco Expressway flaw exploited after public proof of concept
items.why: F6 investigated an attack on internet-exposed devices, though Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use.
items.action: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; no workaround) and restrict TCP 4371-4372 to cluster peers.

items.title: Apache says Roller remote code execution flaw is exploited
items.why: Apache states the unauthenticated XML-RPC flaw in versions 4.0.0 to 6.1.4 is being exploited.
items.action: Upgrade Apache Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping and restart; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.

items.title: Critical Java flaw 'Java4Shell' fixed; CISA urges immediate patching
items.why: Affects Java 17, 21, 25 and 27 on x86-64; Rapid7 does not report exploitation in the wild.
items.action: Inventory every Java runtime, including bundled ones, and install the fixed releases (for example 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1), internet-facing systems first. See the CISA alert for interim controls.

items.title: F5 fixes five critical NGINX flaws; proof-of-concept code is public
items.why: F5 does not report exploitation in the wild, but public PoC code exists for the HTTP/2 flaws.
items.action: Upgrade NGINX Open Source to 1.30.7 (stable) or 1.31.9 (mainline), or NGINX Plus to the fixed release in F5's advisory; if you cannot, set http2 off in affected server blocks (NGINX 1.25.1+) or remove the http2 parameter from listen directives. Check ingress-nginx against its own advisories.

items.title: Malicious agent-framework releases on PyPI steal cloud and CI credentials
items.why: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 were removed within about an hour; how they were published is not yet known.
items.action: Search lockfiles, CI logs, images and virtualenvs for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 and pin to 1.26.0. Where either ran, rotate every secret in that environment and review Azure managed identities and federated credentials.

items.title: Hydro-Québec asks 1.7 million customers to reset passwords
items.why: The company says intruders used passwords already used elsewhere and internal systems were not compromised.
items.action: Hydro-Québec customers: log in to the Espace client from the official site, reset your password if prompted, and never reuse it elsewhere. Ignore password-reset links in emails or texts.
